name: Anonymous German bookkeeping sync
description: A solo tool that syncs Stripe into German bookkeeping tools. The Acquire listing does not name the company or give a product site.

mentions.evidence: Self-reported, with a P&L attached. $158K revenue and $120K profit over the last 12 months. Last month $16.4K revenue and $12.5K profit. $126.4K ARR, up 168% a year. 500–999 customers, 1–3% churn, founded May 2022. Asking $523K, which is 4.5x profit.
mentions.indieAngle: German bookkeeping rules are the product. The listing is the note. There is no company name to build on.

whyItPrints: It is the glue between Stripe and the books a German company already keeps. One person, a P&L attached to the listing, and an asking price.
whyThisMatters:
Stripe does not speak the file format a German bookkeeper wants. This listing is a one-person tool that does that translation. The Acquire page does not name the company and does not give a product site. I am not guessing either one.

The seller attached a P&L. The last twelve months show revenue and a larger share of it as profit. The last month is busier than that yearly pace. Customer count is a range, a few hundred to just under a thousand. Churn is described as low. Founded in May 2022. The asking price is a few times the profit, not a startup multiple. All of that is the seller's paper. It is not a Stripe connection on this site.

You pay so the payout lands in the German books without a weekend of exports.

Five hundred to just under a thousand customers is a range, not a headcount I checked. Churn in the listing is one to three percent. The asking price is tied to profit, not to a story about growth.
